patch.summary:
Choose incident.io only if your buying job matches “Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/user; on-ca” rather than ThorData's shape. Choose ThorData only if your buying job matches “Budget proxy + scraper tooling — Residential from $2/GB (1GB pack); Web Scraper API credit” rather than incident.io's shape. Workflow advantage: incident.io leans incident-oncall; ThorData leans web-data-collection. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: incident.io is Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/user; on-call add-on +$10–$20/user. Does not outrank PagerDut; ThorData is Budget proxy + scraper tooling — Residential from $2/GB (1GB pack); Web Scraper API credit packs from ~$30..
- Company-size focus: incident.io (small-business, mid-market) vs ThorData (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: incident.io-leaning incident-oncall vs ThorData-leaning web-data-collection.
- Researched limits: incident.io — On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor; ThorData — Brand maturity and enterprise compliance story are thinner than Bright Data / Oxylabs.

Limitations — incident.io: On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor; Does not outrank PagerDuty (8.0) as the incident-oncall award; ThorData: Brand maturity and enterprise compliance story are thinner than Bright Data / Oxylabs; Marketing claims should be validated — score from published packaging, not Fortune-500 slogans.

Poor-fit cases: incident.io is a poor fit when that limitation bites: On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor · ThorData is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Brand maturity and enterprise compliance story are thinner than Bright Data / Oxylabs · Avoid incident.io if you actually need ThorData's motion (Budget proxy + scraper tooling — Residential from $2/GB (1GB pack); Web Scraper )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
